\"om_x100b6e253304a93cb2767e7af226732\", \"senderId\": \"cli_a974499e77fadbdd\", \"createTime\": \"1779505116741\", \"msgType\": \"post\", \"content\": \"🔄 [ 重新审稿] 📋  [审稿报告 → Research Director] \\n [ 审稿报告 ]\\n Overall: 3.5 - Borderline Conference 审稿报告 — Round 10 (Fresh Review) 论文 : Reproducibility Budgets for Open-Weight LLM Evaluation: A Generalizability Theory Study of 7–9B Instruction-Tuned Models\\n Venue : EMNLP 2026 (via ARR)\\n 截止日期 : 2026-05-25\\n Reviewer 编排 : 2 人（R1 方法严谨性 / R2 新颖性与完整性）；Reviewer 3 本轮未分配任务（EMNLP 一般会议标准编排为 2 人）\\n 审稿模式 : Fresh（重新审稿，无上轮记忆） Summary 本文将 Generalizability theory (G-theory) 应用于 LLM 评估方差分解，在 8 个 7–9B 开源指令微调模型和 5 个 benchmark 上交叉 7 个 facets（item, model, precision, prompt, seed, temperature, ordering），生成约 230 万条 binary 评估记录。核心产出是 D-study 可复现性预算：推荐 3-prompt × 3-seed 设计以 178 items 达到 G ≥ 0.80（vs. 单条件设计 552 items），并发现 MC 与 FF benchmarks 的方差结构存在格式相关的差异模式。 Strengths S1  [ 强 ] 实验规模与设计严谨性突出——230 万条记录、7 facets 全交叉、8 模型 × 5 benchmarks 的 factorial design 在 LLM 评估方差分析文献中属最大规模之一。Henderson Method I + 1,000 resample bootstrap CI 的统计方法选择恰当。 S2  [ 强 ] 鲁棒性验证异常充分——9 项独立分析（GLMM complement, REML comparison, probit simulation, null calibration, LOMO, CI method comparison, inter-model agreement, facet specification sensitivity, reduced crossing validation）系统性排除了几乎所有可预见的方法论质疑。论文最突出的技术优势。 S3  [ 强 ] 实用产出具体可操作——D-study budget recommendations（3×3 design with 178 items）和 intermediate design gradient（Table 9: minimal upgrade 2p → standard 4p×4s×2t）为 evaluation practitioners 提供即时可用的决策工具。承诺开源 G-theory pipeline 和 D-study calculator。 S4  [ 中 ] Binary scoring conditionality 的透明处理——§3.5 首次声明、§4.1 text-exact-match 实验佐证（G=0.936 vs 0.007）、Appendix A partial-credit pilot 验证（G 0.76→0.55, ρ=0.26）、§4.3 再次提醒——多次多角度披露远超同类论文水平。 S5  [ 中 ] IRT+G-theory 互补性分析（Table 4）——证明 item selection（IRT）和 protocol optimization（G-theory）正交：IRT 116 items 在 single-condition 下 G=0.457 但 multi-facet 下 G=0.895。值得独立突出的洞见。 S6  [ 中] Subject-level 分析有洞察价值——Table 10 揭示 reasoning-heavy subjects（high_ school_ math: G=0.614）与 knowledge-intensive subjects（international_ law: G=0.930）的显著差异，对 benchmark 设计者有直接参考价值。 Weaknesses Must-Fix（影响接收决定） MF1  [ critical, 强共识 ] D-study item budget 公式不完整，核心贡献不可独立验证 Equation 1 定义 G_ item = σ²_ p / (σ²_ p + σ²_ rel)，其中 σ²_ rel 仅依赖各 facet 条件数，不含 item 数量 n_ p。据此公式 G 与 n_ p 无关，但 Table 4 的 budget（55/178/552 items for G≥0.80）和 Figure 1 的 D-study 曲线明显依赖 item 数。反推显示实际使用了 Spearman-Brown 类公式（G(n) = nG₁/(1+(n-1)G₁)），但论文从未给出。论文实际存在两个不同的 G 指标但只明确定义了一个。D-study 预算是论文的核心实用贡献（标题和摘要的主角），读者无法独立验证关键数字——这是可复现性的根本问题。 → 建议：§3.1 或附录完整给出 D-study 投影公式（含 n_ p），区分 per-item G 和 aggregate-score G，提供从 variance components 到 Table 4 数值的完整计算示例。 MF2  [ critical, 强共识 ] Binary scoring scope 未在 title/abstract 中限定 Title \\\"Reproducibility Budgets for Open-Weight LLM Evaluation\\\" 暗示 budgets 适用于通用 LLM evaluation，但所有 D-study budgets 仅对 binary correctness scoring 有效。Partial-credit pilot 显示 G 从 0.76 降至 0.55（ρ=0.26），text-exact-match 更极端（G=0.936 vs 0.007）。实际 LLM evaluation 中大量场景使用 continuous scoring（MT-Bench, AlpacaEval win rate, LLM-as-judge），论文 budgets 对这些场景无指导价值。§3.5 的声明（\\\"All findings are conditioned on binary correctness scoring\\\"）正确但位置过深，title/abstract 未反映。 → 建议：Title 加 \\\"under Binary Scoring\\\" 或 \\\"for Binary Benchmarks\\\"；Abstract 首处提及 D-study budget 时立即声明 scope。 MF3  [ warning→critical, 共识 with nuance ] Binary scoring 对 D-study projection 精度的系统偏差未量化 Probit simulation 报告 binary 与 continuous variance components 之间 ρ=0.732（excluding residual），top-5 ordering 仅 79% correct，|bias|=0.28–0.37（中等难度 items）。Bootstrap CIs 捕捉 item-sampling variability 但不含 binary scoring 的系统偏差。如果 variance components 因 binary scoring 存在系统偏差，D-study 的具体 item 数推荐可能不准确。R2 指出 null calibration（ratio=1.0008）和 component ordering consistency（100%）说明 relative ranking 稳健，认为严重程度略低于 R1 评估——但双方同意需量化影响。 → 建议：从 probit simulation 的 continuous variance components 计算 D-study projections 并与 binary 版本比较；报告 D-study budget 在 binary vs. continuous 下的差异（绝对 item 数和百分比）。 Should-Fix（影响评分但不一票否决） SF1  [ warning, 强共识] G_ item 与模型比较可靠性的概念鸿沟 论文以 item 为 object of measurement，G_ item 衡量 item 难度在方法论条件下的泛化性。但读者更关心的是模型比较可靠性（model ranking reliability）。σ²_ model 仅 2.8%，G_ model 可能显著低于 G_ item=0.896。论文以 \\\"reproducibility budget for evaluation\\\" 措辞呈现结果，构成 framing mismatch。 → 建议：显式计算 G_ model（models 为 object），讨论 G_ item ≥ 0.80 蕴含（或不蕴含）model ranking reliability 的条件。 SF2  [ warning, 持续分歧——5 轮 ] 相对于 Messing (2026) TEE 的增量贡献定位 R2 认为三个扩展方向（infrastructure facets, cross-benchmark, D-study budgets）均非 methodological advance，novelty 不足。R1 反驳：fully crossed multi-benchmark design 使 infrastructure × methodology interaction 首次可估计，是 design-level 创新；binary data adaptation 非平凡。R1 建议从 critical 降为 should-fix。双方一致认为 IRT+G-theory 互补性（Table 4）是最有价值但被低估的贡献点。 → 建议：将 IRT+G-theory 互补性提升至 Contributions；Positioning 段对三个扩展方向标注方法论层级（methodological extension vs. empirical scale-up）。 SF3  [ warning, 强共识 ] \\\"3.1× item reduction\\\" framing 隐藏 total evaluation 增长 Abstract 和 Contribution C1 强调 item 减少（552→178）但 total evaluations 从 552 增至 1,602（2.9× 增长）。这不是 reduction 而是 resource reallocation。§4.5 的讨论（\\\"trading approximately 3× more evaluations per item for 3× fewer items\\\"）比 Abstract 更诚实。 → 建议：Abstract 和 C1 对称呈现 item reduction (3.1×) 和 total evaluation increase (2.9×)。 SF4  [ warning, 强共识 ] 模型可交换性 out-of-sample 验证不足 LOMO（CV ≤ 1.25%）和 four-model subset check（|ΔG| ≤ 0.029/0.065）是 within-sample stability，非 out-of-sample generalization。72B validation 仅 Qwen2.5 family（共享 tokenizer 和训练方法）。8 个模型的时间同质性（2024-2025 训练周期、training data overlap）可能高估 variance structure 稳定性。 → 建议：获取至少一个 cross-family validation point（如 Llama-3 70B）；更明确限定 budget 推荐适用范围。 SF5  [ warning, 强共识 ] Format-associated pattern 统计支撑不足且占用过多篇幅 n=5 benchmarks, permutation p=0.10, benchmark-level CI 含零 [ -1.7, 5.1]。设计不对称（ordering 仅 MC, prompt 类型不同）是额外 confound。§4.3 约 1 页正文（~ 12.5%）对于 p=0.10 的 exploratory observation 在 8 页限制下偏奢侈。已标注 \\\"exploratory\\\" 处理透明。 → 建议：§4.3 正文压缩至 1 段核心发现，详细讨论移至附录。 SF6  [ warning, 共识 ] Partial-credit pilot 基于单 benchmark 单 model 但结论过于确定 §3.5 写 \\\"D-study budgets do not transfer to finer-grained scoring rubrics\\\"，但仅基于 GSM8K + Llama-3.1-8B。ρ=0.26 的变化幅度足够大，核心 message 不变，但措辞需软化。 → 建议：改为 \\\"preliminary evidence suggests limited transferability\\\"。 SF7  [ warning, R2→R1 部分同意 ] Conclusion 过于简短 当前 Conclusion 约半页，仅复述数字和 binary scoring 限制。缺少 practitioner-oriented 讨论（evaluation harness 整合路径、benchmark 设计者 vs 使用者建议）。R1 认为简短是 8 页限制下合理选择但同意可扩展 1-2 句。 → 建议：扩展至 2-3 段，增加 practical adoption pathway。 SF8  [ warning, R2→R1 部分同意 ] Related Work 缺 evaluation harness 实现文献 未讨论 lm-eval-harness evaluation protocol 与本文 facets 的映射、MMLU-Redux/MMLU-Pro 等变体。 → 建议：Related Work 或 Limitations 增加 1-2 句。 Minor（不影响接收） -  M1 : Abstract 数字密度过高（20+ 数值），核心 message 被淹没（R2-M1, R1 AGREE） -  M2 : Table 3 \\\"prompt\\\" 行 MC/FF 含义不同（MC = prompt×item interaction, FF = prompt main effect），行标签应区分（R2-M2, R1 AGREE） -  M3 : \\\"all others  < 0.1%\\\" 不够精确，建议报告具体数值（R1-M1） -  M4 : 排除 temperature=1.0 可能低估 temperature variance（R1-M2） -  M5 : 单一推理引擎（vLLM 0.9.2），其他引擎可能引入额外 variance（R1-M3） -  M6 : §4.4 Precision Separability 仅 2 句话作为独立 subsection 过短（R2-M4, R1 认为 negative result 简短合理） -  M7 : Figure 1 y 轴字体偏小，Figure 3 legend 字号偏小、灰度可区分性一般（R2-M5 + 视觉审查） Reviewer Consensus [ AGREE ] 以下问题两位 Reviewer 独立提出并在交叉回应中确认一致： 1. - R2 立场 (Should-Fix): 三个扩展方向逐一审视——(i) facet 替换非方法论创新；(ii) 跨 benchmark 增加 scope 但核心发现一致（item 在所有 benchmark 上主导）；(iii) D-study 是教科书内容非方法论贡献。属于 "competent application" 而非 "methodological advance"，excitement 不足。
- R1 立场 (REBUT): 整体贡献超越三个子 claims 的加法——(i) 同时交叉 infrastructure + methodology facets 使二者 interaction 首次可估计（如 precision×temperature = 1.3%），是 design-level 创新；(ii) 跨 benchmark 结果揭示了 heterogeneity（MC item-dominated vs FF distributed），非 "核心发现一致"；(iii) D-study 方法是教科书内容但具体 budget 数字是实证贡献。
- Director 判断: 此分歧反映对 "应用创新 vs 方法论创新" 价值判断的根本差异。R1 论证更有说服力——将 G-theory 系统引入 LLM 评估确实是方法论应用层面的贡献，cross-benchmark heterogeneity 发现也非 trivial。但 R2 的核心质疑有效：excitement 低于 pure methodological innovation，这是限制评分的关键因素。
分歧 2：Model main effect 2.8% 的解读
- R2 立场: Model main effect 仅 2.8% 意味着模型近乎不可区分，模型样本可能过于同质，D-study budgets 泛化性存疑。
- R1 立场 (REBUT): R2 误读了 G-theory。Model main effect 小意味着整体准确率相近（7-9B 同量级 expected），不等于模型 "不可区分"。Model×item interaction（30-36%）才是 ranking 信息来源。D-study 估计 ranking reliability 而非 absolute differentiation——即使 model main effect = 0%，只要 model×item interaction 够大，G 仍可很高。正确的泛化性质疑应关注 model×item interaction 在更多样模型下是否稳定。
- Director 判断: R1 的技术解读完全正确。Model main effect 在 G-theory 中不贡献于 G 系数计算——G 衡量的是 relative standing（ranking），不是 absolute differentiation。R2 的泛化性担忧仍然有效（model×item interaction 可能在更多样模型下改变），但论证角度需修正。


Questions for Authors
Q1. Table 8 的 4 models 是 8 models 子集。是否有能力做 truly held-out 验证——例如用 exp-001 方差分量预测 exp-002 中某个全新 benchmark 的 G 系数？[R1, R2 AGREE]
Q2. Probit simulation ρ = 0.732：能否报告 variance components 的 MAPE 而非仅 rank correlation？对 D-study budget 的具体数字，magnitude accuracy 比 rank preservation 更关键。[R1, R2 AGREE]
Q3. Partial-credit G = 0.55, ρ = 0.26 是基于 GSM8K 单一 benchmark 还是多 benchmark？如仅一个 benchmark，partial-credit 结论的泛化性进一步受限。[R1]
Q4. Table 4 显示 multi-facet 3×3 设计需 1,602 evaluations，单条件设计仅需 552。能否提供具体的 GPU-hours 或 API 成本对比，明确在何种场景下 multi-facet 设计优于单条件设计？[R2]
Q5. 鉴于 partial credit "fundamentally reshapes variance structure"，这些基于 binary scoring 的 budgets 对非 binary 场景（LLM-as-judge, BLEU, F1, rubric-based）的参考价值如何？[R2]

Missing References
以下为两位 Reviewer 共同或各自建议的缺失引用：
1. Saxon et al. (2024) — "Benchmarks as Microscopes: A Call for Model Metrology" (COLM 2024). 与论文的 measurement-theoretic framing 直接互补。[R2]
2. Alzahrani et al. (2024) — "When Benchmarks are Targets: Revealing the Sensitivity of Large Language Model Leaderboards" (ACL 2024). 讨论 leaderboard 排名对评估方法论选择的敏感性。[R2]
3. Oren et al. (2024) — "Proving Test Set Contamination in Black Box Language Models". 可支撑 W7 data contamination 讨论。[R1]
这些问题能否解决呢？

108	For practitioners, the design choice depends on the evaluation bottleneck: the full 1,296-condition design minimizes items (55 items, 71,280 evaluations per model); the recommended 3-prompt $\times$ 3-seed design balances cost and reliability (178 items, 1,602 evaluations)\footnote{The additional conditions require approximately 8 GPU-minutes per model across five benchmarks on a single accelerator, making the multi-facet overhead negligible relative to its diagnostic value.}; single-condition designs require 552 items at minimal per-item cost. Multi-facet designs suit settings where item construction is expensive (e.g., expert-crafted benchmarks); more items under fewer conditions suit compute-constrained evaluation (adoption gradient in Appendix~\ref{app:intermediate_dstudy}). Cross-model projections show budget ratios of 11--22$\times$ across benchmarks (bootstrap CIs all exceed 10$\times$; Appendix~\ref{app:dstudy_cross}), with multi-facet budgets ranging from 71 to 162 items (Table~\ref{tab:dstudy_cross}).
109	
110	\paragraph{Projection assumptions.} Cross-model budgets increase to 93 items because model$\times$item interaction enters relative error variance. Bootstrap CIs (71--162 items) and LOMO analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:robustness}) assess stability. All projections assume the 2024--2025 model generation; the 72B extension (\S4.6) provides preliminary support.

113	
114	Within-family analysis (Qwen2.5 3B/7B/72B on MMLU) shows qualitatively invariant variance structure: item difficulty dominates at all three scales (73--83\%, all $G > 0.95$) with consistent facet ranking. The proportional increase at 72B is consistent with the Bernoulli variance ceiling: total variance (0.113) matches $p(1{-}p)$ at grand mean 0.87, compressing all components while item difficulty---the hardest to eliminate---retains the largest share. A crossed 3B$\times$7B$\times$72B design yields model$\times$item = 38.5\% $>$ item = 35.7\%, reflecting expected DIF amplification across a 68--87\% accuracy range ($G_\text{item} = 0.720$; three models insufficient). 116	\paragraph{Robustness checks.} Three MMLU resamples yield CV = 3.1\%; treating models as fixed increases $G$ by 0.077--0.113, confirming conservative budgets (\S\ref{sec:model_facet}; seven additional analyses in Appendix~\ref{app:robustness}).

9	
10	\paragraph{Estimator robustness.} We compare Henderson Method~I with restricted maximum likelihood (REML-EM, 500 iterations, practical convergence $\Delta < 0.003$ percentage points). All variance components differ by $<$0.5 percentage points between estimators. The largest discrepancy occurs on the residual component (0.47pp); all substantive components (item, model$\times$item, model) differ by $<$0.3pp. Henderson Method~I is preferred for our balanced designs because it produces unbiased estimates without distributional assumptions \cite[Ch.~12]{brennan2001generalizability}.
11	
12	\paragraph{Probit simulation.} A probit simulation matched to our 1,296-condition design confirms that Henderson Method~I recovers variance component rankings from dichotomized data (Spearman $\rho = 0.732$ between binary and continuous rankings, excluding residual; \texttt{item\_id} dominant in all 100 replications; top-5 ordering correct in 79\% of replications). Bias analysis by difficulty stratum shows $|\text{bias}| = 0.28$--$0.37$ for items with $p \in [0.5, 0.8]$, where the Bernoulli variance ceiling $p(1{-}p)$ is largest. This analysis covers the observed accuracy range ($p \in [0.3, 0.9]$); extreme-difficulty items ($p < 0.3$ or $p > 0.9$) are rare in our sample ($<$8\% of items) and may exhibit larger deviations. Henderson Method~I absorbs this Bernoulli-inherent variance into the residual, explaining inflated bias near medium difficulty; systematic component ordering is robustly recovered across all replications. Binary scoring inflates residual variance by absorbing the Bernoulli $p(1{-}p)$ ceiling, which enters $\sigma^2_\text{rel}$ and increases D-study item requirements. Within a matched probit simulation, binarization increases D-study budgets by approximately 36\% (99 $\to$ 135 items for $G \geq 0.80$), driven by residual inflation (16\% $\to$ 41\%) and item variance compression (50\% $\to$ 32\%). Facet$\times$item interactions---the components entering $\sigma^2_\text{rel}$---are best preserved under binarization (MAPE = 12.8\%, range 8.7--17.5\%), while residual variance inflates as expected from Bernoulli $p(1{-}p)$ noise (MAPE = 156\%). D-study budgets derived from binary data are therefore conservative: continuous-scored designs would require equal or fewer items for the same $G$ threshold. Null calibration (ratio $= 1.0008$) confirms that this conservatism does not distort relative component magnitudes.

Bootstrap CIs capture item-sampling variability conditional on these 8 specific models; model-level stability is assessed separately via LOMO (below). The agreement indicates that the dependence structure introduced by item-level bootstrap resampling (which creates $\sim$127 unique items per 200-item resample) does not materially distort interval estimates. Stratified resampling by subject (10 subjects $\times$ 20 items) produces CIs within 4\% of simple item-level bootstrap, confirming that the within-subject dependence structure does not materially affect interval estimates.

The random-facet assumption is therefore robust to facet classification.

No single model removal changes $G$ by more than 0.030 (GSM8K, removing Gemma-2-9B). Item-related variance rankings are preserved in all 40 subsets. \appendix
\section{Additional Robustness Analyses}
\label{app:robustness}

We report nine robustness analyses that verify the stability of the variance decomposition under alternative analytical choices.

\paragraph{GLMM complement.} A generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with marginal logit link produces variance component rankings that perfectly preserve all seven grouped component orderings ($\rho = 1.0$) relative to Henderson Method~I \cite{jiang2018bayesian, tuerlinckx2006glmm}. This confirms that the linear variance decomposition is robust to the binary outcome distribution.

\paragraph{Accuracy-range stability.} The \texttt{item\_id} variance share remains stable across subsets with mean accuracy from 0.62 to 0.72 ($r = -0.048$). This rules out distortion from binary floor or ceiling effects at observed accuracy levels.

\paragraph{Estimator robustness.} We compare Henderson Method~I with restricted maximum likelihood (REML-EM, 500 iterations, practical convergence $\Delta < 0.003$ percentage points). All variance components differ by $<$0.5 percentage points between estimators. The largest discrepancy occurs on the residual component (0.47pp); all substantive components (item, model$\times$item, model) differ by $<$0.3pp. Henderson Method~I is preferred for our balanced designs because it produces unbiased estimates without distributional assumptions \cite[Ch.~12]{brennan2001generalizability}.

\paragraph{Probit simulation.} A probit simulation matched to our 1,296-condition design confirms that Henderson Method~I recovers variance component rankings from dichotomized data (Spearman $\rho = 0.732$ between binary and continuous rankings, excluding residual; \texttt{item\_id} dominant in all 100 replications; top-5 ordering correct in 79\% of replications). Bias analysis by difficulty stratum shows $|\text{bias}| = 0.28$--$0.37$ for items with $p \in [0.5, 0.8]$, where the Bernoulli variance ceiling $p(1{-}p)$ is largest. This analysis covers the observed accuracy range ($p \in [0.3, 0.9]$); extreme-difficulty items ($p < 0.3$ or $p > 0.9$) are rare in our sample ($<$8\% of items) and may exhibit larger deviations. Henderson Method~I absorbs this Bernoulli-inherent variance into the residual, explaining inflated bias near medium difficulty; systematic component ordering is robustly recovered across all replications. Binary scoring inflates residual variance by absorbing the Bernoulli $p(1{-}p)$ ceiling, which enters $\sigma^2_\text{rel}$ and increases D-study item requirements. Within a matched probit simulation, binarization increases D-study budgets by approximately 36\% (99 $\to$ 135 items for $G \geq 0.80$), driven by residual inflation (16\% $\to$ 41\%) and item variance compression (50\% $\to$ 32\%). Facet$\times$item interactions---the components entering $\sigma^2_\text{rel}$---are best preserved under binarization (MAPE = 12.8\%, range 8.7--17.5\%), while residual variance inflates as expected from Bernoulli $p(1{-}p)$ noise (MAPE = 156\%). D-study budgets derived from binary data are therefore conservative: continuous-scored designs would require equal or fewer items for the same $G$ threshold. Null calibration (ratio $= 1.0008$) confirms that this conservatism does not distort relative component magnitudes.

\paragraph{CI method comparison.} Bootstrap (1,000 item-level resamples with replacement) and delete-1 jackknife confidence intervals agree closely: width ratios range from 0.96 to 1.04 across all variance components. Bootstrap CIs capture item-sampling variability conditional on these 8 specific models; model-level stability is assessed separately via LOMO (below). The agreement indicates that the dependence structure introduced by item-level bootstrap resampling (which creates $\sim$127 unique items per 200-item resample) does not materially distort interval estimates. Stratified resampling by subject (10 subjects $\times$ 20 items) produces CIs within 4\% of simple item-level bootstrap, confirming that the within-subject dependence structure does not materially affect interval estimates.

\paragraph{Facet specification sensitivity.} Treating temperature and ordering as fixed (rather than random) facets changes $G_\text{item}$ by only 0.37 percentage points (all-random: 0.820 vs.\ fixed temperature+ordering: 0.824). The small difference reflects the negligible temperature$\times$item (0.65\%) and ordering$\times$item (0.54\%) variance shares. The random-facet assumption is therefore robust to facet classification.

\paragraph{Leave-one-model-out (LOMO).} Across all 40 leave-one-model-out subsets (8 models $\times$ 5 benchmarks), $G_\text{item}$ ranges from 0.833 to 0.919, with CV $\leq$ 1.25\% per benchmark. No single model removal changes $G$ by more than 0.030 (GSM8K, removing Gemma-2-9B). Item-related variance rankings are preserved in all 40 subsets. Table~\ref{tab:lomo_full} reports per-benchmark stability. This supports treating models as exchangeable within the target universe of 7--9B instruction-tuned models (\S\ref{sec:model_facet}).

\centering
\caption{LOMO stability across five benchmarks (8 models $\times$ 5 benchmarks = 40 subsets).}
\label{tab:lomo_full}
\scriptsize

\toprule
Benchmark & $G_\text{full}$ & CV (\%) & Max $|\Delta G|$ & Most impactful \\
\midrule

1	\section{Experiments}
2	
3	All experiments use open-weight 7--9B parameter models evaluated with vLLM~0.9.2 on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU (96GB) with binary correctness scoring.
4	
5	\subsection{Single-Model Baseline}
6	
7	We first establish the variance structure within a single model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) on MMLU to isolate methodological facet contributions before introducing cross-model variation.
8	
9	\paragraph{Design.} The G-study crosses six facets: 200 items $\times$ 3 numerical precisions (BF16, FP16, FP32) $\times$ 6 prompt templates $\times$ 6 random seeds $\times$ 3 temperature levels (0.0, 0.3, 0.7) $\times$ 4 answer orderings, yielding 259,200 binary observations. Variance components are estimated via Henderson Method~I with bootstrap confidence intervals (1,000 resamples).
10	
11	\paragraph{Results.} Under binary scoring, item difficulty (\texttt{item\_id}) accounts for 58.4\% of total variance, with the residual term contributing 23.1\%. All main facet effects are negligible ($<$1\% each): precision 0.9\%, prompt template, temperature, seed, and ordering each $<$0.5\%. The interesting structure appears in item-conditional interactions: prompt$\times$item is the largest at 5.5\%, followed by seed$\times$item (4.7\%), precision$\times$item (3.3\%), temperature$\times$item (2.9\%), and ordering$\times$item (0.8\%). This pattern indicates that methodological choices do not shift performance uniformly across items; instead, specific items are differentially sensitive to specific facets---prompt template variation produces the largest item-conditional effect.
12	
13	The resulting generalizability coefficient is $G_\text{item} = 0.936$, indicating that 200 items under multi-facet conditions produce highly reliable rankings. A D-study projection shows $G \geq 0.80$ is achievable with as few as 55 items in this multi-facet design.
14	
15	For text-exact-match scoring (requiring verbatim string matches), the variance structure shifts dramatically: temperature dominates at 79.7\% of variance, and $G_\text{item}$ collapses to 0.007. This metric-conditional divergence motivates our exclusive use of binary correctness for the remaining analyses.
16	
17	\subsection{Cross-Model Variance}
18	
19	Extending to eight models (BF16 subset, 460,800 records), Table~\ref{tab:cross_model} shows that item difficulty drops from 58.4\% to 37.9\%, while model$\times$item interaction emerges at up to 36\%. The model main effect is 3--5\% (MC) and 9--11\% (FF), confirming that models differ primarily in \emph{which items} they find difficult rather than in overall ability level. Contamination implications are discussed in \S\ref{sec:limitations}.
20	
21	\begin{table}[t]
22	\centering
23	\caption{Variance decomposition for the cross-model MMLU design (8 models, BF16, 460,800 records). Components estimated via Henderson Method~I. $G_\text{item} = 0.896$.}
24	\label{tab:cross_model}
25	\small
26	\begin{tabular}{lr}
27	\toprule
28	Component & Var.\% \\
29	\midrule
30	\textbf{item\_id} & \textbf{37.9} \\
31	\underline{model$\times$item} & \underline{30.2} \\
32	residual & 25.0 \\
33	model & 2.8 \\
34	prompt$\times$item & 2.5 \\
35	model$\times$prompt & 1.6 \\
36	all others (each) & $<$0.1 \\
37	\bottomrule
38	\end{tabular}
39	\end{table}
40	
41	\subsection{Exploratory: Format-Associated Variance Patterns}
42	\label{sec:format_conditional}
43	
44	We extend to five benchmarks (three MC: MMLU, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag; two FF: GSM8K, MATH) using exp-002 (8 models $\times$ BF16 $\times$ 2 temperatures $\times$ 6 prompts $\times$ 6 seeds $\times$ 4 orderings $\times$ 200 items). The factorial design is not fully symmetric: ordering applies only to MC, and prompt templates serve format-specific functions, potentially confounding format comparisons. Per-benchmark details---including HellaSwag and ARC exceptions, FF residual analysis, and difficulty dispersion as a variance predictor---are in Appendix~\ref{app:format_details}. All format-associated findings are conditional on binary scoring (\S\ref{sec:binary}).

47	\centering
48	\caption{Format-associated variance structure across five benchmarks (exp-002, 8 models). Variance components (\%) per benchmark; MC = multiple-choice, FF = free-form. 75	\subsection{Precision Separability}
76	
77	Under binary scoring, BF16 and FP16 are functionally interchangeable ($<$0.1\% interaction \cite{yuan2025layercast}); under text-exact-match, a precision$\times$temperature interaction emerges at 1.3\%, consistent with \S4.1. Precision need not be controlled for binary evaluation at BF16/FP16 \cite{shanmugavelu2024floating}.
78	
79	\subsection{Design-Dependent Reproducibility Budgets}
80	
81	How many items does a given evaluation design need to achieve a target reliability? We translate variance components into item budgets via D-study projections.
82	
83	Table~\ref{tab:dstudy} compares evaluation designs at the $G \geq 0.80$ threshold using single-model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) MMLU variance components. The multi-facet design (1,296 conditions per item) achieves $G = 0.936$ at 200 items and requires only 55 items for $G \geq 0.80$. A single-condition design reaches only $G = 0.592$ at 200 items and requires 552 items---a 10.0$\times$ budget ratio stable across subset sizes (CV = 1.9\%).
84	
85	\begin{table}[t]
86	\centering
87	\caption{D-study reproducibility budgets under different evaluation designs (single-model, MMLU). Total evals = items $\times$ conditions.}
88	\label{tab:dstudy}
89	\scriptsize
90	\begin{tabular}{lcrrrc}
91	\toprule
92	Design & Cond. & $n_{G{\geq}.80}$ & Total & $G_{200}$ & $G_{116}$ \\
93	\midrule
94	Multi-facet & 1{,}296 & \textbf{55} & 71{,}280 & \textbf{.936} & --- \\
95	Single-cond. & 1 & 552 & 552 & .592 & .457 \\
96	IRT+multi & 1{,}296 & --- & 150{,}336 & --- & .895$^\ddagger$ \\
97	\midrule
98	IRT baseline & --- & 116 & 116 & --- & .457$^\dagger$ \\
99	\bottomrule
100	\end{tabular}
101	
102	\vspace{2pt}
103	{\scriptsize $^\dagger$\,PSN-IRT 116 items \cite{zhou2026irt} under single-condition: $G = 0.457$. $^\ddagger$\,Same 116 items under multi-facet: $G = 0.895$.}
104	\end{table}
105	
106	\citet{zhou2026irt}'s IRT-selected 116 items yield $G = 0.457$ under single-condition but $G = 0.895$ under multi-facet conditions, demonstrating that IRT item selection and G-theory protocol optimization are orthogonal and complementary. An internal consistency check using four-model subsets confirms projection stability ($|\Delta G| \leq 0.029$ for MC, $\leq 0.065$ for FF; Table~\ref{tab:forward_pred}).
107	
108	For practitioners, the design choice depends on the evaluation bottleneck: the full 1,296-condition design minimizes items (55 items, 71,280 evaluations per model); the recommended 3-prompt $\times$ 3-seed design balances cost and reliability (178 items, 1,602 evaluations)\footnote{The additional conditions require approximately 8 GPU-minutes per model across five benchmarks on a single accelerator, making the multi-facet overhead negligible relative to its diagnostic value.}; single-condition designs require 552 items at minimal per-item cost. Multi-facet designs suit settings where item construction is expensive (e.g., expert-crafted benchmarks); more items under fewer conditions suit compute-constrained evaluation (adoption gradient in Appendix~\ref{app:intermediate_dstudy}). Cross-model projections show budget ratios of 11--22$\times$ across benchmarks (bootstrap CIs all exceed 10$\times$; Appendix~\ref{app:dstudy_cross}), with multi-facet budgets ranging from 71 to 162 items (Table~\ref{tab:dstudy_cross}).
109	
110	\paragraph{Projection assumptions.} Cross-model budgets increase to 93 items because model$\times$item interaction enters relative error variance. Bootstrap CIs (71--162 items) and LOMO analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:robustness}) assess stability. All projections assume the 2024--2025 model generation; the 72B extension (\S4.6) provides preliminary support.
111	
112	\subsection{Preliminary Scale Validation}
113	
114	Within-family analysis (Qwen2.5 3B/7B/72B on MMLU) shows qualitatively invariant variance structure: item difficulty dominates at all three scales (73--83\%, all $G > 0.95$) with consistent facet ranking. A crossed 3B$\times$7B$\times$72B design yields model$\times$item = 38.5\% $>$ item = 35.7\%, reflecting expected DIF amplification across a 68--87\% accuracy range ($G_\text{item} = 0.720$; three models insufficient). The out-of-sample 72B provides preliminary within-family evidence that variance structure is stable across a 24$\times$ parameter range within Qwen2.5; cross-family generalization remains untested.
115	
116	\paragraph{Robustness checks.} Three MMLU resamples yield CV = 3.1\%; treating models as fixed increases $G$ by 0.077--0.113, confirming conservative budgets (\S\ref{sec:model_facet}; seven additional analyses in Appendix~\ref{app:robustness}).

We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a fully crossed design with up to seven facets across eight open-weight instruction-tuned models (7--9B parameters) and five benchmarks, totaling approximately 2.3 million evaluation records. Preliminary validation across a 3B--72B parameter range confirms stable variance structure within one architecture family. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator for evaluation design optimization.
